messages.text:
"THE LITTLE THINGS – Cozy Life Simulator

Create a fully playable, first-person 3D cozy life simulation game inspired by cottagecore aesthetics, cozy Japanese-inspired interiors, and the simple pleasures of everyday living.

The player lives in a charming home in a peaceful neighborhood and can freely explore, interact with objects, complete household chores, cook, garden, shop, adopt stray cats, and enjoy relaxing movie nights.

1. Home and Exploration

Create a beautifully decorated, fully interactive home with a kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom, laundry area, and backyard. Allow players to walk around, pick up objects, open cabinets, use appliances, sit on furniture, and customize their home.

2. Coffee Making and Cooking

Include a functional espresso machine and coffee station. Players can grind beans, pull espresso shots, steam milk, and make lattes, cortados, cappuccinos, americanos, mochas, and affogatos. Include interactive cooking, baking, and recipe discovery. Players can sell homemade coffee and food to neighbors for money.

3. Vintage Magnavox Kitchen TV

Place a tiny vintage Magnavox CRT television on the kitchen counter, with a DVD player and a collection of physical DVD cases beside it. Allow players to pick up DVDs, inspect covers, insert discs, and play movies. Include original animated fantasy films inspired by whimsical Japanese animation, cozy storytelling, and magical adventures. Players can collect more DVDs, watch movies while drinking coffee or eating breakfast, and enjoy the nostalgic television glow.

4. Gardening

Create an interactive backyard garden where players can plant seeds, water plants, grow vegetables, fruits, herbs, and flowers, and harvest ingredients. Use homegrown produce in recipes or sell it to neighbors.

5. Cat Adoption

Stray cats should occasionally visit the backyard. Players can leave food, gain their trust, pet them, and eventually adopt them. Allow players to name multiple cats, feed them, buy treats and toys, play with them, and watch them explore and sleep around the house. Give every cat a unique personality.

6. Household Chores

Include interactive dishwashing, laundry, folding clothes, vacuuming, sweeping, wiping counters, and cleaning. Washing machines, dryers, and sinks should have functional interactions.

7. Grocery Shopping

Create an explorable local grocery store where players can purchase food, coffee beans, milk, syrups, baking ingredients, household supplies, laundry detergent, cat food, treats, toys, and gardening supplies. Purchased items should appear in the player's inventory.

8. Neighborhood and Economy

Include friendly neighbors, a grocery store, bakery, park, and local shops. Allow players to sell coffee, baked goods, and garden produce, complete neighbor requests, earn money, and purchase furniture, decorations, appliances, and supplies.

9. Daily Life and Atmosphere

Include a day/night cycle, changing weather, and seasons. Players can enjoy rainy mornings, make coffee, feed their cats, tend the garden, shop, cook, and relax with movies. Include ambient sounds such as rain, birds, coffee machines, appliances, and cat purring.

10. Visual Style

Use beautiful stylized 3D graphics with cozy cottagecore aesthetics, warm lighting, natural sunlight, soft pastel colors, wooden textures, plants, charming furniture, detailed food, and adorable cats.

IMPORTANT GAMEPLAY REQUIREMENTS

This must be a genuinely playable first-person 3D simulator, not just a decorative environment. All major activities must have functional mechanics, interactive objects, animations, inventory systems, and meaningful progression.

Overall vision: Create a peaceful, immersive everyday-life simulator where players can make specialty coffee, cook, maintain their home, grow a garden, adopt stray cats, shop, make money, collect DVDs, and enjoy cozy movie nights on their tiny vintage kitchen television. There should be no combat, stressful survival mechanics, or pressure to complete activities. Let players enjoy life at their own pace.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

"THE LITTLE THINGS – Cozy Life Simulator

Create a fully playable, first-person 3D cozy life simulation game inspired by cottagecore aesthetics, cozy Japanese-inspired interiors, and the simple pleasures of everyday living.

The player lives in a charming home in a peaceful neighborhood and can freely explore, interact with objects, complete household chores, cook, garden, shop, adopt stray cats, and enjoy relaxing movie nights.

1. Home and Exploration

Create a beautifully decorated, fully interactive home with a kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom, laundry area, and backyard. Allow players to walk around, pick up objects, open cabinets, use appliances, sit on furniture, and customize their home.

2. Coffee Making and Cooking

Include a functional espresso machine and coffee station. Players can grind beans, pull espresso shots, steam milk, and make lattes, cortados, cappuccinos, americanos, mochas, and affogatos. Include interactive cooking, baking, and recipe discovery. Players can sell homemade coffee and food to neighbors for money.

3. Vintage Magnavox Kitchen TV

Place a tiny vintage Magnavox CRT television on the kitchen counter, with a DVD player and a collection of physical DVD cases beside it. Allow players to pick up DVDs, inspect covers, insert discs, and play movies. Include original animated fantasy films inspired by whimsical Japanese animation, cozy storytelling, and magical adventures. Players can collect more DVDs, watch movies while drinking coffee or eating breakfast, and enjoy the nostalgic television glow.

4. Gardening

Create an interactive backyard garden where players can plant seeds, water plants, grow vegetables, fruits, herbs, and flowers, and harvest ingredients. Use homegrown produce in recipes or sell it to neighbors.

5. Cat Adoption

Stray cats should occasionally visit the backyard. Players can leave food, gain their trust, pet them, and eventually adopt them. Allow players to name multiple cats, feed them, buy treats and toys, play with them, and watch them explore and sleep around the house. Give every cat a unique personality.

6. Household Chores

Include interactive dishwashing, laundry, folding clothes, vacuuming, sweeping, wiping counters, and cleaning. Washing machines, dryers, and sinks should have functional interactions.

7. Grocery Shopping

Create an explorable local grocery store where players can purchase food, coffee beans, milk, syrups, baking ingredients, household supplies, laundry detergent, cat food, treats, toys, and gardening supplies. Purchased items should appear in the player's inventory.

8. Neighborhood and Economy

Include friendly neighbors, a grocery store, bakery, park, and local shops. Allow players to sell coffee, baked goods, and garden produce, complete neighbor requests, earn money, and purchase furniture, decorations, appliances, and supplies.

9. Daily Life and Atmosphere

Include a day/night cycle, changing weather, and seasons. Players can enjoy rainy mornings, make coffee, feed their cats, tend the garden, shop, cook, and relax with movies. Include ambient sounds such as rain, birds, coffee machines, appliances, and cat purring.

10. Visual Style

Use beautiful stylized 3D graphics with cozy cottagecore aesthetics, warm lighting, natural sunlight, soft pastel colors, wooden textures, plants, charming furniture, detailed food, and adorable cats.

IMPORTANT GAMEPLAY REQUIREMENTS

This must be a genuinely playable first-person 3D simulator, not just a decorative environment. All major activities must have functional mechanics, interactive objects, animations, inventory systems, and meaningful progression.

Overall vision: Create a peaceful, immersive everyday-life simulator where players can make specialty coffee, cook, maintain their home, grow a garden, adopt stray cats, shop, make money, collect DVDs, and enjoy cozy movie nights on their tiny vintage kitchen television. There should be no combat, stressful survival mechanics, or pressure to complete activities. Let players enjoy life at their own pace.

## Objective
- Complete “The Little Things,” a cozy first-person life simulator, and validate it in-browser with a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include home exploration, coffee and cooking, a vintage Magnavox TV/DVDs with original films, gardening, cat adoption, chores, shopping, neighborhood economy, and day/night/weather/season atmosphere.
- Keep it unhurried, with no combat or survival pressure; finish without questions and note assumptions briefly.
- Save check screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js via CDN, HTML/CSS UI, localStorage persistence, and procedural low-poly environments.
- Organize play around a cottage, garden, and village market.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive interface, start screen, scenes, mechanics, persistence, controls, and render/update handling.
- Fixed duplicate `travel()` and interaction target direction logic.
- Fixed a `window` name collision by renaming the helper to `addWindow`; `node --check game.js` passes.
- Started the local server at `http://localhost:3002`; browser loads the game without console errors.
- Captured and inspected `little-things-check.jpg` at 1280×800.

### Active
- Validate core gameplay interactions in the browser and fix any issues found.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test core interactions in-browser, including coffee, travel, gardening, shopping, cat adoption, chores, and the TV/DVDs.
2. Fix any issues, then capture and inspect a final JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game scenes, mechanics, controls, and persistence.
- `index.html`: Interface, styling, and Three.js entry point.
- `little-things-check.jpg`: Current browser check screenshot.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture wrapper.
- `start.sh`: Existing server startup wrapper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser session has existing localStorage data; the displayed satchel count was 9.
- Screenshot captured at 1280×800; browser console showed zero errors after the `addWindow` fix.

## Objective
- Complete “The Little Things,” a cozy first-person life simulator, and validate core gameplay in-browser.
- Capture and inspect a final JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Include home exploration, coffee and cooking, a vintage Magnavox TV/DVDs with original films, gardening, cat adoption, chores, shopping, neighborhood economy, and day/night/weather/season atmosphere.
- Keep gameplay unhurried, without combat or survival pressure; finish without questions and note assumptions briefly.
- Save check screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js via CDN, HTML/CSS UI, localStorage persistence, and procedural low-poly environments.
- Organize play around a cottage, garden, and village market.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive interface, scenes, mechanics, persistence, controls, and render/update handling.
- Fixed duplicate `travel()`, interaction target direction logic, the `window` name collision, the start-screen overlay, and initial camera yaw.
- Confirmed DVD interaction and playing an owned film updates `localStorage`.
- Verified garden transition and gardening: entered `HOME · BACK GARDEN`, planted tomatoes, and watered them; saved garden and inventory state was confirmed in `localStorage`.
- `node --check game.js` passed previously; browser console showed zero errors.

### Active
- Validate remaining core gameplay interactions in the browser, especially market navigation/shopping, cat adoption, chores, and coffee.
- Capture and inspect a final JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- No confirmed blocker; market navigation and remaining interactions are not yet verified.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks for shopping, cat adoption, chores, and coffee; verify market transition.
2. Capture and inspect the final JPEG screenshot, then check console errors and repository status.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game scenes, mechanics, controls, persistence, and travel logic.
- `index.html`: Interface, styling, and Three.js entry point.
- `little-things-check.jpg`: Existing inspected browser screenshot.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture wrapper.
- `start.sh`: Server startup wrapper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier `git status --short` showed untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `little-things-check.jpg`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.
- Local server is at `http://localhost:3002`; browser localStorage key is `littleThings`.
- Start the game with `playwright-cli eval 'document.querySelector("#startBtn").click()'`; clicking the “Come on in” text did not match.
- Browser movement requires direction-aware navigation; the garden was reached by moving to its prompt, then pressing E. Garden bed interaction and planting/watering worked.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version
